'''Maya Alejandra Fernández Allende''' (born 27 September 1971<ref>{{Cite web|date=2012-01-16|title=Portal de Ñuñoa|url=http://www.nunoa.cl/municipalidad/curriculum/mfernandez.tpl|access-date=2021-03-28|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120116115801/http://www.nunoa.cl/municipalidad/curriculum/mfernandez.tpl|archive-date=2012-01-16}}</ref>) is a Chilean biologist, veterinarian, politician, and a member of the [[Socialist Party of Chile]] (PS) who served as [[Ministry of National Defense (Chile)|Minister of National Defense of Chile]] between 2022 and 2025. She has served as a deputy of the Republic, representing the 10th district, Metropolitan Region, since March 2018. In her first legislative year, she presided over the Chamber of Deputies between March 2018 and March 2019. From 2022 to 2025, she served as Minister of Defence in the Cabinet of [[President of Chile|President]] [[Gabriel Boric]].

== Early life and education ==
Born in Chile to Cuban diplomat Luis Fernández Oña and [[Beatriz Allende|Beatriz Allende Bussi]], she is a grandchild of the Chilean President [[Salvador Allende]].<ref name="qe">{{Cite web|last=Artaza|first=Francisco|date=2022-01-24|title=Quién es Maya Fernández, la nueva ministra de Defensa de Gabriel Boric|url=https://www.latercera.com/politica/noticia/quien-es-maya-fernandez-la-nueva-ministra-de-defensa-de-gabriel-boric/XD4G4O2QRZF2DPV5C4ZKGESX6M/|access-date=2022-01-25|website=La Tercera}}</ref> She and her family had to emigrate to [[Cuba]] due to the [[1973 Chilean coup d'état|military coup of 11 September 1973]] against her grandfather,<ref>{{Cite news|last=Vogt|first=Jürgen|date=2022-01-23|title=Neues Kabinett in Chile: 14 Frauen in der Regierung|language=de|work=Die Tageszeitung: taz|url=https://taz.de/!5829976/|access-date=2022-01-25|issn=0931-9085}}</ref> staying on the island until she was 21 years old. She returned to Chile in 1990, settling permanently in 1992.<ref name="fa">{{Cite web|last=Chile|first=BCN Biblioteca del Congreso Nacional de|date=2020|title=Maya Alejandra Fernández Allende. Reseñas biográficas parlamentarias|url=https://www.bcn.cl/historiapolitica/resenas_parlamentarias/wiki/Maya_Alejandra_Fernández_Allende|access-date=2021-03-28|website=bcn.cl}}</ref> The same year she began studying biology at the [[University of Chile]]. She subsequently also studied veterinary medicine at the same university and obtained a [[Bachelor of Science|BSc]] in both.<ref name="mf">{{Cite web|title=Maya Fenández|url=https://progressivepost.eu/author/maya-fernandez|access-date=2021-03-28|website=The Progressive Post|language=en-US}}</ref>

== Political career ==
In 1992 she joined the Socialist Party of Chile.<ref name="fa"/> In the 2008 municipal elections, she was elected councilor for the Nuñoa commune, which she stayed until 2012.<ref name="mf"/> During the presidency of [[Michelle Bachelet]] between 2006 and 2012, she worked in the [[Ministry of Foreign Affairs (Chile)|Ministry of Foreign Relations]].<ref name="qe"/> In the municipal elections of 2012, she ran for the mayorship of [[Ñuñoa]] for the Socialist Party on the [[Concertación|Concertation]] list.<ref>{{Cite news|date=2012-12-05|title=Au Chili, le centre gauche retrouve l'espoir de revenir au pouvoir en 2013|language=fr|work=Le Monde.fr|url=https://www.lemonde.fr/international/article/2012/12/05/au-chili-le-centre-gauche-retrouve-l-espoir-de-revenir-au-pouvoir-en-2013_1800116_3210.html|access-date=2021-03-28}}</ref> The favorite to win the elections was [[Pedro Sabat]], who had been serving as mayor of Nuñoa for the past 16 years.<ref name="ce">{{Cite web|date=2012-11-13|title=Chilean electoral tribunal overturns Fernández Allende's mayoral victory|url=http://www.theguardian.com/world/2012/nov/13/chile-fernandez-allende-recount-election|access-date=2021-03-28|website=the Guardian|language=en}}</ref> Fernandez at first won the elections by a slim margin of twenty votes, a result which was appealed by Sabat, who in turn came out victorious after a recount which gave him a thirty-vote lead.<ref name="ce"/>

=== Member of Parliament ===
In the [[2013 Chilean general election|2013 parliamentary elections]], Fernández ran for the position of deputy for the 21st district, which includes the communes Nuñoa and [[Providencia, Chile|Providencia]] from the metropolitan communes of Santiago. From 11 March 2014 to 11 March 2018, she represented the 21st district for the PS in the [[Chamber of Deputies of Chile|Chamber of Deputies]].<ref name="fa"/> In the [[2017 Chilean general election|2017 parliamentary elections]], she was re-elected deputy, this time for the newly created [[District 10 (Chamber of Deputies of Chile)|District 10]] of the Metropolitan Region.<ref name="fa"/> On the 11 March 2018, she became president of the Chamber of Deputies.<ref name="fa"/> She left office in March 2019.<ref name="fa"/>

=== Minister of Defense ===
From March 2022 to March 2025, Fernández served as the [[Ministry of National Defense (Chile)|Minister of Defense]] in the Cabinet of [[Gabriel Boric]].<ref name="fa"/> Referring to the military coup in which her grandfather and former [[President of Chile]] was killed, she saw the role of the [[Chilean Army|Chilean Military]] to defend Chile as a country and not to get involved in internal security.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Palma |first=Natalia |date=17 April 2022 |title=Ministra Maya Fernández Allende: "El rol de las FF.AA no es el orden público" « Diario y Radio Universidad Chile |url=https://radio.uchile.cl/2022/04/17/ministra-maya-fernandez-allende-el-rol-de-las-ff-aa-no-es-el-orden-publico/ |access-date=2022-09-20 |website=Radio Universidad de Chile |language=es-ES}}</ref>

In January 2025, she accompanied Gabriel Boric on his [[Operación Estrella Polar III|journey]] to the [[Amundsen-Scott South Pole Station]].<ref name="oe">{{cite web |url=https://prensa.presidencia.cl/comunicado.aspx?id=294446 |title=Operación Estrella Polar III concreta con éxito histórica visita del Presidente de la República, Gabriel Boric Font, y su comitiva al Polo Sur |date=2025-01-03 |access-date=2026-07-14}}</ref> It was the first trip by a sitting president of [[Latin America]] to the [[South Pole]].<ref name="oe"/>

Fernández resigned from the Cabinet on 10 March 2025 amid controversy over the attempted sale of a property that had belonged to her late grandfather, [[President of Chile|President]] [[Salvador Allende]], to the government for use as a museum.<ref>[https://efe.com/en/latest-news/2025-03-11/chilean-defense-minister-resigns-amid-controversy-over-failed-purchase-of-allendes-home/ Chilean Defense Minister resigns amid controversy over failed purchase of Allende’s home], EFE:, ''[[EFE:]]'', 11 March 2025</ref> She was accused by political opponents of violating the Constitution. "She committed a serious offense against the Constitution and the laws. No minister of state can enter into contracts with the state and the minister did so," Congresswoman [[Camila Flores]], of right-wing [[Chile Vamos]], told a press conference. In a related development three weeks later, on 3 April, the [[Constitutional Court of Chile|Constitutional Court]] ordered Fernández's aunt, [[Isabel Allende Bussi]], to forfeit her seat in the [[Senate of Chile|Senate]] for having violated Article 60 of the [[Constitution of Chile|Constitution]], which prohibits office-holders from engaging in state contract negotiations.<ref>[https://en.mercopress.com/2025/04/04/chile-s-constitutional-court-ejects-isabel-allende-from-senate Chile's Constitutional Court ejects Isabel Allende from Senate], MercoPress, ''[[Merco Press]]'', 04 April 2025</ref> Fernández and Allende, along with other descendants of Salvador Allende, are joint owners of his residence at 392 Guardia Vieja Street in the [[Santiago]] suburb of [[Providencia, Chile|Providencia]].

== Personal life ==
She is the daughter of Cuban diplomat and politician of the [[Communist Party of Cuba|Cuban Communist Party]] Luis Fernández Oña and surgeon [[Beatriz Allende|Beatriz Allende Bussi]],<ref name="qe"/> and the youngest granddaughter of former President [[Salvador Allende]].<ref name="qe"/> She is also a niece to Senator [[Isabel Allende (politician)|Isabel Allende]].<ref name="fa"/> Being a [[volunteer firefighter]] of Nuñoa,<ref name="qe"/> she is married to Tomás Monsalve Egaña and has two children.<ref name="fa"/>
